paper.title: Fully sequential Gaussian process regression for preference learning

settings.name_in_paper: Global optimization with noisy pairwise comparisons (preference learning) via fully sequential GP moment-matching
unmapped: Observation is sign(f(z1)-f(z2)+xi) with xi ~ N(0, sigma^2) (probit comparison model)
f is deterministic and continuous; f - mu^0 - c_* lies in the RKHS of the prior kernel Sigma^0 for some unknown constant c_*
Kernel approximation width W_r^2 = O(r^{-a}) with a > 1 (rate-driving assumption)
Design space compact, convex, uncountable subset of R^d
settings.definition_quote: we may choose two design points $x,x'\in\mathcal{X}$ and make a noisy observation of only the \textit{sign} of $f(x) - f(x')$ ... $D_s = s\cdot(f(z_1) - f(z_2) + \xi)$ ... We assume $\xi\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2)$ with $\sigma > 0$.

symbols.a_w: exponent in the kernel approximation-width condition W_r^2 = O(r^{-a}), a > 1

conditions: Assumption 3.1: X compact convex uncountable subset of R^d; f deterministic continuous; mu^0, Sigma^0 continuous, Sigma^0 PSD with strict Cauchy-Schwarz for distinct points
Assumption 5.1: f - mu^0 - c_* in RKHS of Sigma^0 for some constant c_*
Assumption 5.2: approximation width W_r^2 = O(r^{-a}) with a > 1
tuning: proposal satisfies B^n(z1,z2) >= chi * sup B^n for fixed chi in (0,1)
randomized bridge with rho^n = diam/sqrt(log(n+e)), Lambda^n = log log(n+e^e)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Suppose that we are in the situation of Theorem \ref{thm:consistency}. Let $\hat{x}^n$ be an $\mathcal{F}^n$-measurable element of $\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}} \mu^n(x)$. Then, there exists a deterministic $N_1$ such that $\mathbb{E}(\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}}f(x) - f(\hat{x}^n)) = O(\sqrt{\log n}\cdot n^{-\frac{a-1}{2(a+1)}})$ for $n \geq N_1$.

results.notes: Expected simple regret after n comparisons (n = T). For Matern kernel with nu > d/2, a = 2nu/d giving O(n^{-(nu-d/2)/(2nu+d)} sqrt(log n)) (stated in text, not a separate result). Quantity chosen as simple_regret since it is expected suboptimality of the recommended point.

symbols.a_w: exponent in the kernel approximation-width condition W_r^2 = O(r^{-a}), a > 1

conditions: bound is on sup_{x,x'} |(mu^n(x)-mu^n(x')) - (f(x)-f(x'))|^2 (squared uniform statistical error of pairwise differences)
tuning: proposal satisfies B^n >= chi * sup B^n for fixed chi in (0,1)

source.label: thm:consistency
source.quote: Let Assumptions \ref{a1}, \ref{a3} and \ref{a4} hold, and suppose that $(z^n_1,z^n_2)$ is determined using the DOVE policy ... Then, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $\sup_{x,x'\in\mathcal{X}}|\ell_{x,x'}\Delta^n|^2 = o((\log n)^{2+\varepsilon} n^{-\frac{a-1}{a+1}})$ almost surely.

results.notes: Paper states little-o; recorded with O notation (weaker). Quantity is squared estimation error of pairwise differences, not regret.

cited_results.setting_description: Classical GP regression / Bayesian optimization with Gaussian (uncensored) observations, Matern kernel with smoothness nu, dimension d
